messages:
maria: heads-up — perf spike in host ingress this morning. p95 CPU for host-proxy jumped ~35% -> ~78% at ~08:03 on a subset of pods. traces look like lots of tiny gRPC frames plus heavy tokenization work. link to quick flame: https://paste.example.com/ingress-flame

sam: can you paste the flame top hotspots or a quick breakdown?

maria: quick top from the flame (truncated):
```
parse::tokenize 46%
ingress::frame_dispatch 22%
kvcache::lookup 10%
grpc::recv_small_writev 8%
syscall::writev 6%
```

jess: wow — syscall/writev noise from tiny writes. did we ship any kernel selection or batching heuristics yesterday?

maria: we rolled kernel-hints patch yesterday (kernel chooser fallback). traffic has a lot of short sequences right now (chatty clients) — suspect batching heuristics now produce lots of small writev batches, increasing syscall overhead prior to tokenization.

ryen: kvcache metrics also show miss rate jump (2% -> 12%) for the affected route. maybe fragmentation of keys per connection leading to cold lookups.

sam: quick experiment idea: increase ingress coalesce window (2ms -> 10ms) and enable proto_merge to aggregate small gRPC payloads before tokenization. that should reduce number of writev syscalls and produce larger token batches for kernel selection.

maria: starting canary with the following config on 3 pods:
```
ingress:
  coalesce_window_ms: 10
  proto_merge: true
  token_batch_hint: 64
```

infra-bot: deploy started: host-proxy/canary-3 in us-west-2 (3 pods) — rollout id r-2026-08-03-0815.

jess: any immediate canary metrics? errors?

maria: quick numbers after ~12m: canary p95 CPU dropped ~35% -> ~40% (toward baseline), writev syscall rate down ~60%, kvcache hit rate improved slightly. no client errors or increases in tail latency yet.

ryen: this aligns with hypothesis: fewer tiny frames -> runtime picks wider vectorized kernels for decode instead of scalar slowpath. we should instrument kernel selection per request to confirm.

sam: agreed. action items:
- keep canary for 2h and monitor tail latencies and errors
- add telemetry to runtime exposing kernel_id and seq_len per request
- update batching heuristics to consider recent seq-length distribution (sliding window) so coalesce_window adapts
- try a kvcache prefetch on cold connections to reduce miss storms

maria: adding to eng-runtime board and opening a PR to add kernel telemetry + canary config. will post results after the 2h run. thanks all.

sam: :thumbsup:

maria: tagging @oncall in case anything regresses overnight.
